justification: Both show low-relief animal or creature figures carved in profile on a tall upright stone with figures stacked in vertical zones, but the specific content diverges sharply: A is dominated by a single large frontal-mouthed, fanged composite creature with scrolled, interlocking curvilinear ornament and a hooked snout, while B presents a repeated row of small crouching quadrupeds above a woven/net band, plus separate slender striding animals and a long-necked bird-like creature. Nothing in the specific postures, attributes or combinations matches beyond the generic fact of relief animals on a slab, and the drawing conventions (dense scroll-work and bulging volumetric heads vs. flat, angular, silhouette-like outlines) are quite unlike.
